# Repository guide

## Project structure

- `conference-companion/` is a dependency-free browser application built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Keep it dependency-free unless the user explicitly asks for a tooling change.
- `index.html` and `app.js` implement the itinerary; `recordings.html` and `recordings.js` implement the media library. Shared presentation lives in `styles.css`, and time-based behavior lives in `timeline.js`.
- `.openai/hosting.json` identifies the hosting project. Do not deploy or change the hosted project unless the user explicitly requests it.

## Generated files and data

- `conference-companion/sessions.js` is generated by `refresh-sessions.mjs` from the root schedule export plus the official session directory. Run the refresh script only when intentionally synchronizing schedule data; it performs network requests and rewrites `sessions.js`.
- `conference-companion/dist/server/index.js` is generated by `build.mjs` and is tracked. After changing a bundled HTML, JavaScript, CSS, or image asset, rebuild it and include the generated worker change.
- Preserve the itinerary schema and browser-storage migrations when changing `itinerary.js` or itinerary state. Update the verification expectations when an intentional data or schema change makes them stale.

## Implementation conventions

- Match the existing plain JavaScript style: browser code uses IIFEs and globals under `window`; Node utilities use ES modules and built-in modules only.
- Escape untrusted or schedule-derived values before inserting them into HTML.
- Preserve accessible names, keyboard behavior, focus management, reduced-motion handling, and responsive layouts when changing the UI.
- When a browser asset changes, bump its matching cache-busting query string in each HTML entry point that loads it.
- Preserve unrelated worktree changes. Do not rewrite generated or data files unless the task requires it.

## Validation

- Syntax-check every changed JavaScript file with `node --check <path>`.
- After changing bundled assets, run `node conference-companion/build.mjs` before the project verification so the tracked worker matches its sources.
- Run `node conference-companion/verify-itinerary.mjs` for changes to the application, schedule, itinerary, build output, or related markup.
- Treat `refresh-sessions.mjs` as an explicit data-refresh operation, not a routine test.
